prose.text: This subject covers how ZPA trusted networks relate to Client Connector. Criteria fields and forwarding profile network types are in [[doc:references/zcc/trusted-networks.md]] and [[doc:references/zcc/forwarding-profile.md]].

zcc-defines-criteria.statement: Zscaler Client Connector identifies a trusted network by criteria defined for it on the Trusted Networks page, and a forwarding profile can select several predefined trusted networks.

quotes: To have Zscaler Client Connector identify one of your organization's trusted networks, you must first define conditions for that network as criteria that Zscaler Client Connector uses for verification.
Predefining the Trusted Network Criteria for your networks on the Trusted Networks page allows you to select multiple trusted networks in a forwarding profile.

policy-menu-source.statement: The trusted networks offered when building a ZPA access policy rule are the ones configured in the Client Connector Portal or Admin Console.

quotes: Make sure you have configured your Trusted Network Criteria within the Zscaler Client Connector Portal. The trusted networks you configure in the Zscaler Client Connector Portal appear in the drop-down menu.
The trusted networks you configure in the Zscaler Admin Console appear in the drop-down menu.

zpa-objects-are-zcc-networks.statement: The read-only trusted network records ZPA returns are the trusted networks configured on the Client Connector side.
zpa-objects-are-zcc-networks.conditions: Inference: the rule menu is fed from the Client Connector configuration and the provider points its trusted network documentation at the Client Connector article; no source states that a ZPA `networkId` equals a Client Connector identifier.

send-result-setting.statement: A Client Connector forwarding profile's ZPA action has a Send Trusted Network Result to ZPA setting, described by the Client Connector API as indicating whether it is enabled.

expect.description: Indicates whether Send Trusted Network Result to ZPA is enabled.

id-correspondence.title: Whether a ZPA networkId equals the identifier of the Client Connector trusted network
id-correspondence.detail: The Client Connector trusted network has a `guid` and the ZPA trusted network has a GUID-style `networkId`. No source states they are the same value. Compare both lists for one network in a tenant that uses both.
id-correspondence.blocks: saying a ZPA networkId can be read from a Client Connector record

signal-path.title: How and when Client Connector reports the trusted network result to ZPA
signal-path.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "When a match occurs, ZCC signals to ZPA at session establishment: this user is on Trusted Network X. ZPA policy evaluation happens at session establishment and per-request." The Client Connector API has a Send Trusted Network Result to ZPA setting, but no source describes the exchange, its timing, or re-evaluation. Capture the tunnel setup and a network change in a lab tenant.
signal-path.blocks: saying when a trusted network change takes effect in ZPA policy

policy-effects.title: What ZPA policy can do differently for users on a trusted network
policy-effects.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "When a user's ZPA session is established from a known trusted network, ZPA can apply different policy logic, for example routing through a local Private Service Edge or relaxing authentication requirements for specific apps." Preferring matching Private Service Edges is documented ([[zpa.trusted-networks.service-edge-groups:prioritize-matching]]); relaxed authentication is not stated in any captured source.
